title: Safety sentinel patterns for staged deployments — field notebook
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight field notebook collecting pragmatic sentinel patterns we can attach to staged rollouts (canary, micro-release, A/B) to detect early functional regressions, quality drift, latency/cost regressions, and privacy/leak signals. Not intended as final policy — meant as working examples the console team and oncall can iterate quickly.

Context and assumptions:
- Applies to LLM-powered features routed via Redwood API/Console (hosted + dedicated + private).
- We assume access to token-level latency, per-route error breakdowns, prompt/response length distributions, model variant tags, and sampling of inputs/outputs for automated checks.
- Privacy: sampled outputs must scrub PII when stored for eval. See privacy playbook (linked artifact).

High-level sentinel categories (quick map):
1) Health sentinels — binary/systemic failures (5xx, model OOM, node disconnect)
2) Latency/KPS sentinels — token-level p50/p95/p99 latency, cold-KV spikes
3) Cost/efficiency sentinels — tokens-per-second, batching delta, quantization revert
4) Quality sentinels — eval set regressions, reranker score drops, hallucination spikes
5) Safety/Policy sentinels — toxic content rate, user complain volume, privacy leakage indicators
6) Behavioral sentinels — sudden shift in output length, repetition rate, stop-token anomalies

Pattern: Lightweight sentinel recipe (one per sentinel)
- Name: short id
- Signal source(s): metrics (Prometheus), traces (Jaeger), sample-checker (eval runner), logs
- Aggregation window: 1m / 5m / 1h (explicit)
- Baseline: rolling 7-day median + MAD or rolling 24h p50/p95; prefer robust stats over simple mean
- Trigger criteria: absolute and relative thresholds (both) + minimum sample count
- Escalation: slack channel, page, auto-fallback route, auto-sampler of recent traffic for analysis
- Playbook: immediate operator steps + follow-ups + owner

Example sentinel (latency tiering):
- Name: latency-p99-token-route
- Sources: metric route.token_latency.p99, traceID sampling
- Window: 5m aggregation, compare to 7-day rolling p99
- Trigger: p99 > baseline * 1.6 AND p99 > 400ms AND requests > 50/min
- On trigger: post to #release-orchestra (with small payload), create incident draft (template), route 50% of traffic to fallback model variant (cost-aware) for 10m, increase sampling of outputs to 10% for quality checks
- Owner: serving-runtime oncall until acknowledged

Example sentinel (quality — reranker drift):
- Name: rerank-top1-drop
- Sources: reranker.top1-score.mean per cohort, client A/B buckets
- Window: 1h rolling, compare to previous 24h
- Trigger: drop > 8% absolute OR relative drop > 18% with >100 evals
- On trigger: mute rollout progression, notify product and solutions-eng, snapshot prompts and top-5 candidates for manual review, run regression harness against golden set

Safety sentinel (toxicity):
- Name: safety-toxic-rate
- Sources: safety-detector.rate, user-report-rate (support tickets tagged toxic), manual moderation counts
- Window: 1h / 6h
- Trigger: toxic-rate > baseline + 0.25% absolute OR user-reports > 10x expected per cohort
- On trigger: reduce exposure to human-only review for high-risk cohorts, escalate to safety lead, stash sampled outputs (PII scrubbed) and run targeted eval with updated classifier thresholds

Behavioral sentinel (repetition):
- Name: repetition-blowup
- Sources: n-gram-repeat-rate, entropy-per-token
- Window: 10m
- Trigger: > 3x baseline repeat-rate AND outputs > 1% of requests flagged
- Action: route to smaller generation length, switch to alternative decoding strategy (top-k) and alert SRE/Product

Operational patterns and guardrails:
- Dual-threshold approach: require both relative AND absolute threshold to avoid noise from tiny baseline values.
- Min-sample gating: no action if sample count < N (configurable per sentinel). Default N=50 for user-visible features.
- Silent vs loud sentinels: some sentinels create internal notes (silent) vs oncall pages (loud). Classify by worst-case user impact.
- Canary progression stages: pilot (0.1% synthetic traffic), micro (1–5%), cohort (10–25%), full (100%). Each stage requires specific sentinel checks to be green for 24h before progressing.
- Canary rollback windows: 5m quick rollback policy for severe signals (latency >1s p99, >1% error rate), 1h for moderate signals.

Playbook templates (short):
- Incident template (auto-fill): ID, sentinel name, window, baseline, triggered value, routes affected, immediate action taken, owner, next steps.
- Communication snippet (for product/CS): short summary of what happened, who is impacted, mitigation in place, ETA for fix, link to incident doc.

Testing and rehearsal ideas:
- Synthetic cohort injection: run scheduled synthetic traffic targeted at canary slices to assert sentinel sensitivity. Keep separate from production user cohorts and flag synthetic.
- Chaos scenarios: CPU/GPU leak, file-system saturation, burst cold-starts. Measure sentinel recall/precision.
- Quarterly calibration: tweak thresholds to maintain false positive rate < 1/month for all loud sentinels.

Tooling and implementation notes (practical):
- Metrics: rely on high-cardinality Prometheus metrics tagged by model, route, cohort, customer-tier. Leverage derived metrics pipeline for robust baselines.
- Sampling: store 1% of outputs in secure eval cluster with PII scrub; escalate sample rate to 10% automatically when quality sentinels trigger.
- Rollout control: Console must expose quick rollback button + automated fallback routing policy per feature. Implement feature-level TTL for automatic revert if no operator activity after 30m on loud incidents.
- Runbooks: keep short, link full runbook per sentinel ID. Operators must annotate incident resolution steps to feed back into runbook.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to incorporate customer-specific baselines for Dedicated (customers might have different p99). Proposed: per-customer baselines with minimum sample requirements.
- Mapping of sentinels to product owner — need canonical ownership table.
- Privacy: finalize scrub script for sampled outputs (PHI/PII filter list).
- Automation: should some sentinels auto-fallback vs require manual confirmation? Default: noisy or high-risk auto-fallback disabled; high-confidence infra failures can auto-fallback.

Examples of quick queries and knobs (ops cheat sheet):
- p99 query (example PromQL): rate(route_token_latency_ms_p99[5m]) / 1000 -> compare to 7d rolling baseline (stored in TSDB-rollups)
- sample fetch: SELECT * FROM eval_samples WHERE route = 'chat-complete' AND created_at > now() - interval '10 minutes' LIMIT 200;
- rollback command (console quick action): POST /api/rollouts/{id}/rollback {"reason":"sentinel:latency-p99-token-route"}

Short diary entries (field notebook excerpts):
- 2025-01-20: micro-release for q3-reranker triggered rerank-top1-drop twice; root cause: training job switched tokenizer padding; lowered p95 threshold and added tokenizer mismatch sentinel.
- 2025-01-28: repetition-blowup fired during cold-cache warm-up after infra patch; mitigation: temporarily increased KV-cache population target and disabled aggressive batching for 15m.

Attachments / checklist before promoting a canary stage:
- Baseline computed and sanity-checked (yes)
- Safety and quality sentinels configured in console (yes)
- Oncall roster notified with staggered checks (yes)
- Rollback and fallback routes validated (yes)
- Sample storage for outputs enabled with scrub (yes)

Notes to self (Lena):
- Convert the sentinel recipes to Console UI templates (cards) so PMs can attach them to a rollout with a single click.
- Build a small repo of synthetic scenarios for each sentinel and add nightly smoke tests.

End of notebook entry.

(If this doc is useful, we should split: 1) sentinel templates (machine-readable), 2) operator runbooks (one per loud sentinel), 3) sample queries and alert dashboards.)
